sources: SUNDAY NOV 8 2026 RUN. US cash markets SHUT all weekend, so this is a VERIFICATION AND CARRY run: every price tile still reads the FRIDAY NOV 6 CLOSE and no new price data exists. The value is unchanged at 0.00 against a 0.50 trigger, so there is still NO RECESSION SIGNAL, but the tile is now a live measurement again rather than a carry. Note this is consistent with unemployment FALLING to 4.1 pct in the October report. TWO - THE YIELD CURVE TILE IS NOW A FETCHED PRINT, NOT A COMPUTED ONE. FRED T10Y2Y has published NOV 6 AT 0.35, updated Nov 6 16:03 CST, which exactly matches the 0.35 computed by hand last run from the 4.86 ten-year and 4.51 two-year closes. Series reads 0.35 Nov 6, 0.38 Nov 5, 0.32 Nov 4, 0.34 Nov 3, 0.32 Nov 2, 0.38 Oct 30. Against 0.38 a week ago the arrow stays DOWN - bear flattening off the hot payrolls, still comfortably positive, nowhere near inversion. THE BIG OPEN QUESTION IS STILL OPEN - THE NOV 6 HY OAS PRINT HAS NOT LANDED. THIS IS THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES THE WEEK and it is due MONDAY NOV 9: back toward 335-340 means the 348 high was a one-day credit shock tied to the Nov 5 equity drop, at or above 348 means the widening is a trend and credit has decoupled from the equity recovery. Nothing in this weekend run resolves it. BREAKEVEN CONFIRMED, NOT CHANGED. FRED T5YIFR NOV 6 AT 2.17 PCT, updated Nov 6 16:03 CST, same print as last run. Against 2.22 a week ago the arrow stays DOWN - the five-basis-point crack that finally came through on Friday with crude under 100. An independent Nov 6 post-market summary confirms VIX 25.64 minus 9.01 pct, S&P 500 7,376.86 plus 0.31 pct, TEN-YEAR 4.86 PCT plus 2bp, TWO-YEAR 4.51 PCT plus 5bp, Brent 97.76, WTI 90.34, DXY 102.28, gold futures 4,079.50 minus 0.83 pct. Those Brent and DXY readings sit 3 cents and 4 hundredths from the tiles carried from yesterday (97.79 and 102.32), which is ordinary close-source variance, so the TILES ARE HELD UNCHANGED for continuity rather than nudged. Most expensive gap on the board. PICTURE: NOTHING MOVED BECAUSE NOTHING COULD MOVE - THE BOARD IS FROZEN ON FRIDAY'S SPLIT AND MONDAY RESOLVES IT. The real economy is unambiguously strong: payrolls plus 165k against 59k expected, unemployment DOWN to 4.1 pct, claims 189k near a 57-year low, ISM accelerating to 55.5, sentiment jumping to a three-month high, conditions still loose at minus 0.46, and the Sahm rule now confirmed at 0.00 on a fresh October print. The stress is entirely on the price side: HY at a new local high of 348bp, the two-year repricing a December hike, the breakeven cracking 5bp lower, crude under 100 - while equity vol faded to 25.64 and the Nasdaq bounced. Credit widening into an equity recovery and a hike being priced into a hot labour market is the divergence that defines this week. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the NOV 6 HY OAS print Monday and whether 348bp was the peak or the start; whether a December hike at 78 pct is a policy mistake into widening credit or a correct read of a 165k payroll; getting a live MOVE print, twenty-one runs blind and never more needed; the NOV 12 NFCI, the first to contain all of this; October CPI mid-month against an easing UMich inflation expectation and a 75.2 ISM prices index; whether the dollar's Friday bid extends or fades back into the flat range; and whether Brent under 100 holds or Hormuz rebuilds a premium.
